source.title: Effects of Non-Uniform Sparsity on Superposition in Toy Models

record.file_problem: The post text is present. Referenced figures and the linked detailed-view document are not included, so their underlying plotted values cannot be extracted.
record.tranche_reason: It applies the ReLU output toy-model setup to new sparsity and importance settings and reports feature representation and superposition results.
record.gate_note: The post also summarizes findings from the cited Toy Models of Superposition paper; those cited findings are not recorded as this study's results. Rows below use only results reported for this post's experiments. The eight instances per scenario are described as different random seeds, but separate numerical seed-level outcomes are not given.
record.test_reason: The post reruns the original ReLU-output toy model (5 features, 2 hidden dims) under non-uniform sparsity. It reports which features are represented, dedicated or superposed, so its own results bear on V1 and V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author finds that non-uniform sparsity yields fewer represented features than uniform sparsity, and that the mix of dedicated and superposed features differs by case. They could not pin down the governing sparsity-importance interaction. The suggestion that importance matters more than sparsity for dedicated dimensions is an intuition drawn from Case 4, not a tested result.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the ReLU output toy-model setup with non-uniform sparsity patterns and four importance/sparsity scenarios; also reports Frobenius Norm as a proxy in an 80-feature, 20-dimension setup and runs eight random-seed instances per scenario.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported representation pattern differs across the four sparsity/importance scenarios; the post notes seed-related exceptions in Case 4.
record.problems: Small toy-model settings are reported (5 input features and 2 hidden dimensions, plus an 80-feature and 20-dimension proxy analysis). The post gives no numerical uncertainty estimates or seed-level results. Some results are described from figures whose underlying plotted values are not present in the supplied text; Frobenius Norm is only a proxy for feature representation.
record.rows_left_out: No separate seed-level rows were possible: the post says there were eight instances per scenario but does not provide their individual outcomes. It also refers to figures and a linked document with further details not included in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Near-orthogonality or angles of directions, regular geometry (polytopes), and the sparsity-dependent phase transition are not measured. Sparsity distribution is fixed per case, not swept.
Only qualitative patterns in four hand-chosen arrangements. No general measure of how importance and sparsity set allocation; the author says the governing combination is unresolved.

record.verdict_notes: Single-author LessWrong post. No numbers beyond feature counts and Frobenius norms, and no uncertainty or seed-level results. Figures are not in the text. The Frobenius rows (R2-R6) are a weak proxy with a mismatched baseline and should not drive verdicts. The record's 'challenges' label for V2 from Case 2 is downgraded to limits_scope: the original paper already shows sparsity trading off against importance, and the sparsest feature here is also the most important.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not quantify the angles or near-orthogonality of represented directions, or establish a regular geometry. It tests non-uniform sparsity scenarios and reports qualitative dedicated-versus-superposed representations.
The post reports qualitative patterns under selected importance/sparsity arrangements, but does not identify a general capacity mechanism or quantify how importance determines allocation.
No alternative cause of polysemantic neurons is tested.
No LLM representations or dictionary recovery are studied.
No SAE features or claims about canonical units are studied.
The post does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.
